searches.query: module federation remote micro frontend classes not working
tailwind styles not applied in remote module loaded by host application

When using Tailwind CSS with a module federation micro-frontend setup, styles from the remote application are purged or not included because Tailwind's content configuration only scans the host app's files, not the remote module's files, so classes used only in the remote are removed by PurgeCSS/JIT.

8: export const description = "Understanding and customizing how Tailwind scans your source files."; 9: 10: ## Overview 11: 12: Tailwind works by scanning your project for utility classes, then generating all of the necessary CSS based on the classes you've actually used. 13: 14: This makes sure your CSS is as small as possible, and is also what makes features like [arbitrary values](/docs/adding-custom-styles#using-arbitrary-values) possible. 15: 16: ### How classes are detected 17: 18: Tailwind treats all of your source files as plain text, and doesn't attempt to actually parse your files as code in any way. 19: 20: Instead it just looks for any tokens in your file that could be classes based on which characters Tailwind is expecting in class names: 21: 22: ```jsx 23: // [!code filename:JSX] 24: // [!code word:bg-blue-500] 25: // [!code word:rounded-full] 26: // [!code word:text-white] 27: // [!code word:text-black] 28: // [!code word:font-medium] 29: // [!code word:text-sm\/6] 30: // [!code word:font-sans] 31: // [!code word:bg-black] 32: // [!code word:bg-white] 33: // [!code word:className] 34: // [!code word:function] 35: // [!code word:children] 36: // [!code word:button] 37: // [!code word:shadow] 38: // [!code word:export] 39: // [!code word:colors] 40: // [!code word:color] 41: // [!code word:black] 42: // [!code word:white] 43: // [!code word:const] 44: // [!code word:blue] 45: // [!code word:return] 46: // [!code word:py-1.5] 47: // [!code word:px-2] 48: export function Button({ color, children }) { 49: const colors = { 50: black: "bg-black text-white", 51: blue: "bg-blue-500 text-white", 52: white: "bg-white text-black", 53: }; 54: 55: return ( 56: 59: ); 60: } 61: ``` 62: 63: Then it tries to generate the CSS for all of these tokens, throwing away any tokens that don't map to a utility class the framework knows about. 64: 65: ### Dynamic class names 66: 67: Since Tailwind scans your source files as plain text, it has no way of understanding string concatenation or interpolation in the programming language you're using. 68: 69: {<>Don't construct class names dynamically} 70: 71: ```html 72: 73:
74: ``` 75: 76: In the example above, the strings `text-red-600` and `text-green-600` do not exist, so Tailwind will not generate those classes. 77: 78: Instead, make sure any class names you’re using exist in full: 79: 80: {<>Always use complete class names} 81: 82: ```html 83: 84: 85: 86:
87: ``` 88: 89: If you're using a component library like React or Vue, this means you shouldn't use props to dynamically construct classes: 90: 91: Don't use props to build class names dynamically 92: 93: ```jsx 94: // [!code filename:JSX] 95: function Button({ color, children }) { 96: return ; 97: } 98: ``` 99: 100: Instead, map props to complete class names that are statically detectable at build-time: 101: 102: Always map props to static class names 103: 104: ```jsx 105: // [!code filename:JSX] 106: function Button({ color, children }) { 107: const colorVariants = { 108: blue: "bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-500", 109: red: "bg-red-600 hover:bg-red-500", 110: }; 111: 112: return ; 113: } 114: ``` 115: 116: This has the added benefit of letting you map different prop values to different color shades for example: 117: 118: ```jsx 119: // [!code filename:JSX] 120: function Button({ color, children }) { 121: const colorVariants = { 122: blue: "bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-500 text-white", 123: red: "bg-red-500 hover:bg-red-400 text-white", 124: yellow: "bg-yellow-300 hover:bg-yellow-400 text-black", 125: }; 126: 127: return ; 128: } 129: ``` 130: 131: As long as you always use complete class names in your code, Tailwind will generate all of your CSS perfectly every time. 132: 133: ### Which files are scanned 134: 135: Tailwind will scan every file in your project for class names, except in the following cases: 136: 137: - Files that are in your `.gitignore` file 138: - Files in the `node_modules` directory 139: - Binary files like images, videos, or zip files 140: - CSS files 141: - Common package manager lock files 142: 143: If you need to scan any files that Tailwind is ignoring by default, you can [explicitly register](#explicitly-registering-sources) those sources. 144: 145: ## Explicitly registering sources 146: 147: Use `@source` to explicitly register source paths relative to the stylesheet: 148: 149: ```css 150: /* [!code filename:CSS] */ 151: @import "tailwindcss"; 152: /* [!code highlight:2] */ 153: @source "../node_modules/@acmecorp/ui-lib"; 154: ``` 155: 156: This is especially useful when you need to scan an external library that is built with Tailwind, since dependencies are usually listed in your `.gitignore` file and ignored by Tailwind by default. 157: 158: ### Setting your base path 159: 160: Tailwind uses the current working directory as its starting point when scanning for class names by default.

content.text:
Root cause: Tailwind only generates CSS for classes it finds by scanning the files listed in your `content` config at build time (tailwind-css/src/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files.mdx, "Which files are scanned" / "Explicitly registering sources", lines 133–156). In an Nx MFE setup, the host's Tailwind build only scans the host's own source paths, so classes used only in the remote module's files never get generated in the host's compiled CSS — and if the remote's own Tailwind build strips out anything not literally present in its files (e.g. classes built via dynamic string interpolation), those get purged too (same doc, "Dynamic class names", lines 65–131).

Fix: make sure each project's `tailwind.config.js` `content` array explicitly includes the remote module's source globs (or vice‑versa), so all libs/apps sharing the Tailwind build are scanned together — the v4 equivalent shown in the doc is `@source "../path/to/remote"`, but for v3.3.3 you add the paths to `content: [...]`.
